newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks end down ahead of company results.
newsitem.headline: China stocks end down ahead of company results.

text.p: China shares ended lower on Wednesday after weeks of sharp gains with investors cautious ahead of the rush of 1996 company results, brokers said.
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index fell 0.17 percent to 73.065 points on turnover of $6.6 million against $7.8 million on Tuesday.
Shenzhen's B share index shed 0.15 percent to 162.25 points as turnover fell to HK$48.4 million ($6.25 million) from Tuesday's HK$73.3 million.

Brokers said most investors were cautious ahead of the April 30 deadline for listed companies to make public their 1996 results, but selling was also light due to fundamental investor confidence in the market.
Fewer than 10 of 87 B share companies listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen have posted 1996 results so far.
"The correction has been expected after the recent rises and market sentiment is good despite falls in the A share market," a Shanghai broker said.
"Investors will be increasingly wary about trading," an analyst with China Guotai Securities said, adding trading was likely to remain quiet over the next few sessions.
In Shanghai, Shanghai Shangling Electric Appliances was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results, falling $0.030, or 7.42 percent, to $0.374 on volume of 393,500 shares.
Shanghai Diesel Engine traded the most on institutional selling, falling $0.010, or 2.08 percent, to $0.470 on volume of 1.1 million shares.

In Shenzhen, beverage producer Shenzhen Shenbao Industrial Co Ltd, which has a joint venture with Pepsi Co Inc, dipped HK$0.23, or 3.87 percent, to HK$5.71 on volume of 16,900 shares, making it the sharpest loser.
Wafangdian Bearing was the most active issue, slipping HK$0.03 to HK$5.03 on trade of 1.67 million shares.
Shanghai's domestic A share index fell 7.657 points, or 0.59 percent, to 1,292.738 points on turnover of eight billion yuan compared with 8.3 billion yuan on Tuesday.
Shanghai New Asia Fast Food lost the most on profit-taking after a financial restructuring was announced, down 8.17 percent to 13.48 yuan on volume of 1.2 million shares.
Shenzhen's A index edged down 2.61 points, or 0.57 percent, to close at 457.15 points on disappointment over 1996 results released by a handful of A share companies on Wednesday, brokers said.
